landing.hero_subtitle: Unified official channel for citizen incident reporting, technical police triage, and real-time tactical vehicle monitoring.

how_it_works.title: How It Works
how_it_works.step1_desc: Complete the online form with details of the event — no need to visit the police precinct. Available 24 hours a day.
how_it_works.step2_desc: Upon submission, you instantly receive an official tracking protocol number. Keep it safe to track your case progress.
how_it_works.step3_desc: Use your protocol number at any time to verify the current stage of police triage and investigation.

services.title: Available Services
services.card_register_desc: Report theft, lost property, threats, and other incidents quickly, without queues and with interactive map location.
services.card_lookup_desc: Track the status and progress of your reported incident in real time using the official protocol code.
services.card_operational_desc: Restricted access for field agents, triage delegates, and centralized dispatch operators.

types.title: What Can Be Reported Online?
types.subtitle: This system accepts non-emergency reports. For life-threatening emergencies or crimes in progress, call 190 immediately.
types.item1_desc: Theft of personal belongings, electronics, vehicles, or other valuable property.
types.item2_desc: Lost documents, wallets, keys, mobile devices, and other personal items.
types.item3_desc: Vehicle collisions or property damage without injured victims.
types.item4_desc: Statements, messages, or physical gestures constituting threats to personal safety.
types.item5_desc: Excessive noise, disruptive neighborhood conduct during quiet hours.
types.item6_desc: Vandalism, graffiti, or malicious destruction of public or private property.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Do I need an account to report an incident?
faq.a1: No. The Citizen Portal is completely public. You do not need to register or log in to submit a report or check your tracking protocol.
faq.q2: What is the difference between this portal and calling 190?
faq.a2: Emergency number 190 is for crimes in progress and immediate danger. This system is for past, non-emergency incidents. If in immediate danger, dial 190.
faq.q3: How long does it take for my report to be reviewed?
faq.a3: Triage timelines vary based on priority. You can monitor progress in real time via protocol. Most standard reports are triaged within 72 hours.
faq.q4: Can I submit a report on behalf of someone else?
faq.a4: Yes, provided you provide the accurate information of the actual claimant. The form allows entering the identity of the person communicating the facts.
faq.a5: It indicates that the investigating authority requested adjustments or clarifications to the reported narrative. Check your protocol for notes.
faq.q6: My incident was rejected. What should I do?
faq.a6: Rejections occur if the event falls outside police jurisdiction or does not constitute a reportable offense. In that case, visit the nearest station.
